newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securitas sees slower '97 profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Securitas sees slower '97 profit growth.

text.p: Swedish security company Securitas said on Wednesday it expected its result for the full-year 1997 to increase 10-15 percent, which would be a slowdown in profit growth from 1996.
But from 1998 it saw profit growth returning to previous years' levels.

The company posted an increase in six-month pre-tax profit to 230 million crowns from 228 million in the corresponding period a year earlier, which was below market expectations of 268 million crowns.

Six-month sales rose 19 percent to 5.08 billion crowns while operating profit before amortization of goodwill edged up four percent to 307 million crowns and earnings per share slipped to 2.26 crowns from 2.28, Securitas said.
Securitas said restructuring in Germany had taken longer than anticipated and affected earnings for 1997.

"The extensive restructuring programme in the German CIT (cash-in-transit) operations is aimed at creating volume and profitability growth on a sustained longterm basis," Securitas said in a statement.
"This work has taken longer than anticipated, thereby affecting earnings performance for 1997."
Securitas said an increase in income of 10-15 percent was anticipated for 1997, which is lower than in previous years.
"Restructuring costs in Germany are gradually abating and starting in 1998 the acquisitions in Britain, France and Sweden will make a positive contribution to profitability," the company said.
"In 1998 the group's earnings performance is thus expected to revert to previous years' levels and long-term trend."
Securitas shares tumbled to 210 crowns on the news, down 11 from their Tuesday close. They were trading three crowns down ahead of the report.
"The result was lower than expectations and the company also lowered its growth forecast to 10-15 percent having previously forecast longterm growth of 20 percent," said a Stockholm-based analyst.
Operations in Sweden, Norway and Denmark continue to show good volume and earnings growth, the company said.
"The CIT operation started in Finland experienced good volume growth but was subjected to significant start-up costs during the period," the company said.
"Operations are expected to generate a positive contribution to earnings from the fourth quarter 1997."
